sentences.text: Rajkumar vs State Of Uttarakhand on 5 June, 2015
Author: Sudhanshu Dhulia Bench: Sudhanshu Dhulia Bail Application No.841 of 2015 in CRLR No.133 of 2015 Hon'ble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Mr. Manish Arora, Advocate, present for the revisionist.
Mr. Raman Kumar Sah, learned Deputy Advocate General assisted by Ms. Shruti Joshi, learned Brief Holder, present for the State of Uttarakhand.

The revisionist has filed present revision against the judgment and order dated 21.04.2015, passed by Ist Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar, passed in Criminal Appeal No.61 of 2009 which arose out of Criminal Case No.27 of 2005, whereby the revisionist was convicted under Section 7(I) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and was sentenced under Section 16 (I)(a)(I) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for Six Months Simple Imprisonment with a fine of Rs.1000/-, with default stipulation.
In compliance of this Court's order dated 26.05.2015, after release on interim bail, the revisionist Rajkumar is present in person before this Court.
He is duly identified by his Counsel Mr. Manish Arora.
Heard learned counsel for revisionist on regular bail and perused the judgment of the courts below.

Considering the overall circumstances of the case, the interim bail granted by this Court vide order dated 26.05.2015, is made absolute, subject to the fact that the revisionist shall not misuse the bail and he shall execute a personal bond and looking to the financial condition of the revisionist he shall furnish one surety of the amount to the satisfaction of the Magistrate/Court concerned.
It is also made clear that sentence of fine imposed by the trial court shall remain suspended.
List this matter in the month of August, 2015 for hearing.
Bail application No.841 of 2015 stands disposed accordingly.

(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.) 05.06.2015 ML Rajkumar vs State Of Uttarakhand on 5 June, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195614659/
